reason: The Book of Ruth demonstrates Hebrew people freely and openly expressing their views throughout the narrative. Ruth explicitly declares her determination to stay with Naomi (1:16-17) in a famous statement of loyalty. Naomi freely offers her counsel to her daughters-in-law about returning to their homes (1:11-13). Boaz engages in direct conversation with Ruth, responding to her requests (2:8-13, 3:11). The elders and townspeople gather at the gate and speak openly, blessing the union and expressing their communal views (4:11-12). Characters exercise agency in voicing their opinions, concerns, and hopes without apparent restriction. The narrative portrays active dialogue and decision-making involving multiple voices.
